claim: Israel is an apartheid state: Arab citizens of Israel are second-class citizens.

heard.quote: Israel imposes a system of oppression and domination against Palestinians across all areas under its control: in Israel and the OPT, and against Palestinian refugees

heard.who: Associated Press, on the Arab minority's reaction to the Nation-State Law, 19 July 2018 (NPR)
heard.quote: see the change as akin to establishing apartheid

answer: Inside Israel's pre-1967 lines the record shows both rights and gaps. Arabs are about a fifth of the population; those with citizenship vote, sit in the Knesset, have served as ministers and as a Supreme Court justice, and in 2021 an Arab party joined the governing coalition. They also lived under military rule until 1966, and today they face documented gaps: poverty about two and a half times the Jewish rate (National Insurance Institute, 2023), unequal municipal services found by the State Comptroller, a record 252 killings in 2025 by the Abraham Initiatives' count, a 2018 law reserving national self-determination to Jews, and a law that bars Palestinian spouses from joining them. Our reading: this is unequal citizenship in a democracy, a serious wrong that Israeli institutions themselves audit and litigate, and not, in our view, the legal crime of apartheid; Amnesty and Human Rights Watch say otherwise (see era6-apartheid-in-law).

facts.text: The National Insurance Institute's 2024 poverty release recorded poverty among Arab families at 37.6 percent in 2024, down from 38.1 percent in 2023, and said that 65.1 percent of the poor come from the periphery and disadvantaged populations, including Arab and Haredi families, almost twice their share of the population (the Jerusalem Post reports the 65.1 percent as the Arab and Haredi share alone). For 2023 the Institute's data, as read by the Israel Democracy Institute, put Arab family poverty at 38.4 percent (the 2024 release says 38.1 percent for 2023) against 15.4 percent for Jewish families.

facts.text: The State Comptroller found gaps in public services and planning: a 2022 audit of five mixed cities found gaps between municipal services to Jewish and Arab residents, and a 2024 audit found that only 49 percent of NIS 80 million allocated for planning in non-Jewish localities under Government Resolution 922 (2016-2020) was used. About 93 percent of Israel's land is held by the state, its Development Authority and the Jewish National Fund.

facts.text: Killings in Arab communities have roughly doubled since 2022, and the counts differ by who counts: the Taub Center counted 220 homicides in the Arab population in 2024 (109 in 2022), the Israel Democracy Institute 239 victims in 2024, and the Abraham Initiatives 252 in 2025, which it called the deadliest year on record. The Israel Police said the Abraham Initiatives' data includes cases in which police thwarted planned murders; the Institute says most such cases are not solved by the police.

facts.text: The Citizenship and Entry into Israel Law (2003, temporary, renewed repeatedly) bars Palestinians from the West Bank and Gaza from receiving Israeli citizenship or residency through marriage; it mainly affects Arab citizens and their spouses. The Supreme Court upheld it 6 to 5 in 2006 and again in 2012. The Knesset failed to renew it in a 59-59 vote in July 2021, and passed it again in March 2022.

contested.text: Whether the Citizenship and Entry Law is a security measure or discrimination. The 2012 ruling upheld the ban on the basis that Palestinian spouses are potential security risks because some had carried out attacks. Human Rights Watch says it is unlawful discrimination that cannot be justified by security interests, and in 2006 Chief Justice Barak, in dissent, wrote that the law violates Arab citizens' right to equality.

sources.title: Israel: High Court Rulings Undermine Human Rights

contested.text: Why killings in Arab communities are rising, and who is responsible. could_not_verify: The Abraham Initiatives' own report and an official police count could not be read; the 2025 killing figures are cited from the Jerusalem Post and its Yahoo copy, which are one source repeated, so that fact has two sites, not three. I did not find a police clearance-rate figure I could read.

I did not find an official source I could read comparing Arab and Jewish local-authority budgets per resident or land allocation per resident; the Comptroller's planning audit and the mixed-cities audit are the closest. Land ownership is cited only as the Comptroller's 93 percent figure for state, Development Authority and JNF land, which is not a split by group.

The current (2026) Knesset's count of Arab members could not be confirmed; the card uses the 2022 election. A current status of the Citizenship and Entry Law after March 2022 (renewals in 2023 and 2024 reported) was not read from a primary page.
Cabinet-level and Supreme Court history beyond Joubran and the 2007 and 2021 ministers was not checked; I did not verify the 2022 appointment of a second Arab justice.
The Knesset page for the Nation-State Law and the Times of Israel page for Joubran load only intermittently for the checker; both were read through fetch.

Reviewer: no source on the card quotes anyone calling Salim Joubran's career a token, only the Jerusalem Post saying Israel has held him up as proof of equal treatment; that 'contested' entry was removed (a position with no quoted holder). The Jurist page body could not be read by the checker; its quote was replaced in the Citizenship Law dispute by an HRW sentence that is on the page.

The Knesset's own English PDF of the Nation-State Law cannot be read by the checker (HTTP 474, no archive copy loads); the law's text is cited from the Jewish Virtual Library's English translation, which says 'unique' where the Knesset translation says 'exclusive'.
not_claimed: This card does not say Arab citizens have full equality, and it does not say they live under apartheid.
It does not say Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza have the same rights as Arab citizens; they do not, see the West Bank card.
It does not excuse military rule until 1966, the budget and planning gaps, or the family-unification ban; they are documented costs to Arab citizens and are facts on this card.
It does not attribute crime figures to any cause; the sources say 88 percent of 2025 victims were shot and describe a loss of basic security, not a cause.

answer_claims.says: Inside Israel's pre-1967 lines the record shows both rights and gaps.

Arabs are about a fifth of the population; those with citizenship vote, sit in the Knesset, have served as ministers and as a Supreme Court justice, and in 2021 an Arab party joined the governing coalition.

They also lived under military rule until 1966, and today they face documented gaps: poverty about two and a half times the Jewish rate (National Insurance Institute, 2023), unequal municipal services found by the State Comptroller, a record 252 killings in 2025 by the Abraham Initiatives' count, a 2018 law reserving national self-determination to Jews, and a law that bars Palestinian spouses from joining them.

Our reading: this is unequal citizenship in a democracy, a serious wrong that Israeli institutions themselves audit and litigate, and not, in our view, the legal crime of apartheid; Amnesty and Human Rights Watch say otherwise (see era6-apartheid-in-law).

skeptic.notes: Round two (re-read CBS, IDI, NII release, Taub, All Israel News, Comptroller 2024, JVL translation, NPR; did not take the writer's word). FIXED: the Knesset quote no longer fails online (the Nation-State Law now cites a translation); killings (fact 8) now carry Taub (220 in 2024, 109 in 2022), IDI (239) and Abraham Initiatives (252), with the police reply and the unsolved-cases finding, so the figure is no longer one NGO and the 'record' is attributed; the Joubran 'token' entry stays removed. NOT FIXED / NEW: [must-fix] Fact 6 is marked a record but did not say what the NII release says: the release says 65.1 percent of the poor come from 'the periphery and disadvantaged populations, including Arab and Haredi families'; the fact (and the Jerusalem Post) turned that into Arab-and-Haredi alone. I reworded to the release. It also gave 38.1 percent for 2023 while the IDI figure is 38.4 percent; now stated. The Jewish rate (15.4) and the 2.5x ratio come only from IDI, which reads 2023 NII data: one reader, and the readers do not carry the 2024 figures. [must-fix] Fact 7: the 49 percent of NIS 80 million and the 93 percent land figure are carried only by the State Comptroller (a government source, which does not count); the three reliable sources carry only the 2022 mixed-cities gap. Make it a record fact or drop the numbers; the 93 percent is not split by group and does not show discrimination. [must-fix] Fact 0: the 21.1 percent is CBS data; IDI and Ynet repeat CBS (I added a wire so they count once), so it needs the record flag or a second measurement. [must-fix] Fact 9 is marked a record but cites a translation on the Jewish Virtual Library, which the card also labels advocacy elsewhere; the Knesset PDF and every other copy returned errors (HTTP 474/403), so no second copy could be compared. NPR does carry 'unique to the Jewish people', so the words match, but the translation is a weak stand-in and 'exclusive' (Knesset) was not re-read by me. I trimmed the government-view and Arab-view clause from the fact (carried by NPR alone; it remains in contested) so the record fact says only what the law and the vote record say. [should-fix] Fact 10: 6-5 (2006) is carried only by HRW (advocacy); Jurist's page body could not be read. Fact 4 'suspended and resumed' not carried. Strongest objections: Palestinian lawyer: the Taub 14:1 Arab-to-Jewish homicide ratio and the unsolved cases are the documented wrong; the card now states counts and the police response but not the ratio. Israeli lawyer: most deaths are criminal violence between crime organisations (now in contested); the CBS-only 21 percent includes East Jerusalem non-citizens (stated).

citer.notes: Round two: re-tied four answer sentences to facts (answer_claims unchanged; the poverty and killings clauses name who counted). Removed nothing further. The poverty clause ('two and a half times the Jewish rate') rests on the IDI reading of 2023 data (38.4/15.4) and is only as strong as that one reader; the answer says National Insurance Institute 2023, which the reworded fact 6 now matches. 'Our reading' still notes that Amnesty and HRW disagree.
